title: Adobe Optimizes Photoshop and Premiere for Arm Windows
summary: Adobe optimizes Photoshop and Premiere Pro performance for Windows on Arm devices
detailed: Adobe's creative apps now run on Arm-based Windows PCs, with Microsoft Photos gaining Adobe-powered editing features.
Adobe has optimized Photoshop, Premiere, After Effects and Substance 3D Painter (beta) for Arm-based Windows PCs, announced at Adobe MAX.
Microsoft Photos on Windows 11 will also gain Adobe-powered editing features and Adobe Express templates, extending Adobe's tools into a built-in Windows app.
Adobe is a software company known for creative tools including Photoshop, Premiere and After Effects, and it is the developer of the applications being optimized for Arm-based Windows PCs.
sentences: Adobe's creative apps now run on Arm-based Windows PCs, with Microsoft Photos gaining Adobe-powered editing features.
Adobe has optimized Photoshop, Premiere, After Effects and Substance 3D Painter (beta) for Arm-based Windows PCs, announced at Adobe MAX.
The optimized applications will be available on the Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.
The optimization brings Adobe's professional creative software to Arm-based Windows hardware, expanding the platforms where these tools run well.
Microsoft Photos on Windows 11 will also gain Adobe-powered editing features and Adobe Express templates, extending Adobe's tools into a built-in Windows app.
Photoshop has been rearchitected to improve responsiveness on Arm-based Windows PCs, and Premiere has an optimized video pipeline for playback, colour correction and rendering.
No specific performance benchmarks have been published alongside the announcement.
Adobe is a software company known for creative tools including Photoshop, Premiere and After Effects, and it is the developer of the applications being optimized for Arm-based Windows PCs.
Microsoft is a technology company that develops the Windows operating system and the Microsoft Photos app that will receive Adobe-powered editing features.
Photoshop's Remove tool uses on-device generative AI to remove unwanted elements and generate replacement content.

Adobe is also developing a compositing-based architecture for Photoshop that will support live filters, HDR and brushing capabilities, with further benchmarking and optimization planned for Windows devices.
A preview of the Microsoft Photos features is expected for Windows Insiders in the coming months.
The collaboration between Adobe and Microsoft was announced at Adobe MAX.
The optimization of Adobe's creative suite for Arm-based Windows PCs places Adobe's software on a growing class of Arm hardware, including the Surface Laptop Ultra powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.
The move positions Windows on Arm as a viable platform for professional creative workloads alongside rival hardware ecosystems.
Users of Arm-based Windows PCs, including the Surface Laptop Ultra, will be able to run Photoshop, Premiere and After Effects in versions optimized for that hardware.
Windows users will also be able to open photos in Adobe Express from Photo Viewer and access Adobe-powered editing in Microsoft Photos.
For Windows users considering an Arm-based laptop for creative work, the announced Adobe optimizations are worth tracking as they roll out to the applications you already use.
